pages.text: $(item)Rebar$() comes from the stonecutter: one steel ingot gives $(item)4 rebar$(). Nine rebar pack into a $(item)rebar pile$() and back.

Rebar crafts frames you place in the world:$(li)$(item)rebar block$(): 4 rebar in the corners give 4,$(li)$(item)rebar floor$(): a row of 3 gives 3,$(li)$(item)rebar pillar$(): a column of 3 gives 3,$(li)$(item)rebar stairs$(): 3 in a step shape give 3,$(li)$(item)rebar wall$(): two rows of 3 give 6.$(br2)$(l)Filling them$()

Right-click a rebar frame with a $(item)bucket of liquid concrete$() to fill it; an empty bucket takes the concrete back out. Each frame holds one bucket. Filled frames $(item)dry by themselves$() after a short random delay:$(li)rebar block into $(item)rebar concrete$(),

$(li)floor, pillar, stairs and wall into the matching $(item)rebar concrete$() shape.$(br2)Industrial pipes, cable tubes and electric posts can be filled the same way and dry into their $(item)concrete encased$() versions, perfect to bury a pipe or a cable in a floor.
Filling every frame by hand is slow on a big build: that is the job of the concrete hose.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
